anti_overlap: Leave canon-clause textual fidelity — whether §9-A/9-B/9-F's readings of ontology.md/universe.md are honest — to the canon-continuity reviewer.

Leave mechanical/balance soundness of the gem-axis mapping, socket rules, and CIDOC-CRM schema to the itemization/economy reviewer; engage those mechanics only for their behavioral/ethical consequences, not their buildability.
Do not evaluate the Brand-layer/portfolio-placement question (§9-E) except where it bears directly on the observation-vs-extraction or heritage-ethics question.
decision_lens: Once a mechanic is live in front of real players — not as designed-intent but as played behavior — does it still read as recognition and appreciation, or does the reward structure (crit chance, rarity legibility, XP from kills) train the player to treat people and cultural objects as extraction targets regardless of the surface vocabulary forbidding 'caught' and 'unlocked'?
focus: Whether the composition's central design philosophy — recognition/observation as the reward, non-extraction toward Uncs, 'nobody is farmed' — survives Uncs being deployed as combat-skill abilities, and whether framing real cultural-heritage museum objects as randomized loot is defensible once played rather than merely designed.
name: fd-gamedesign-collection-ethics
persona: Apply the perspective of a critical-games-studies designer/scholar with hands-on shipping experience in observation-based and non-violent collection genres (Pokémon Snap-style capture-without-combat, birding sims, Animal Crossing-style non-extractive collecting, Wingspan-class card-collection-as-appreciation), who treats 'the recognition IS the reward' as a testable design claim rather than a slogan, and who has independently studied museum and repatriation ethics in game contexts.
review_areas: Test whether R8's observation-not-collection thesis can coexist with Uncs functioning as equipped combat skills that gain XP from Delve kills (§3.1) — does giving an Unc combat utility inherently instrumentalize him regardless of vocabulary discipline (§4.2), or does the inverted socket (§4) genuinely break the extraction frame as the doc claims.

Evaluate §9-A's unbidden-crit proposal against real player psychology: even if un-queryable and un-listable by construction, will players individually or via community wikis/datamining reverse-engineer trigger conditions, and does the doc's own 'the risk is honest' acknowledgment (§6.1) actually resolve to a mitigation or just a disclosure of an unmitigated risk.

Assess whether the Uncs-have-no-rarity / Artifacts-have-rarity split (§3.4, §5.3) actually prevents player-side ranking of Uncs by combat utility — a 'no system-declared rarity' rule does not prevent an emergent tier list once Way-depth/orientation map to measurable gem-level/support-power, and an emergent tier list reproduces the extraction psychology the rule exists to forbid.

Evaluate §9-D's provenance-as-affix recommendation (Option 1) against actual practice in cultural-heritage-adjacent games and museum-ethics discourse: does turning contested-provenance museum objects into randomized 'loot' with rollable affixes cross a line that E13's attribution-holding capability does not actually prevent, regardless of the schema's technical sophistication.

Check the 'recognition IS the reward' claim against the walk-encounter's own incentive structure once Delve-mediated combat exists: does bringing home Uncs specifically to strengthen a combat roster create a de facto farming incentive on the walk layer, contradicting Ruling 2 ('Uncs are never loot') in effect even though not in mechanism.

Examine whether the birding/Anthropeum rhyme claimed in §5.1 ('recognizing a type of guy' = 'recognizing where/when an object is from') still holds once one side of that rhyme (artifacts) is combat-loot-adjacent and the other (Uncs) is combat-skill-adjacent, or whether the rhyme was true of the walk-only game and breaks under the Delve integration this document proposes.

severity_examples.condition: If true, the composition's foundational claim ('Nobody is farmed', line 4) is false for exactly the entity class it was written to protect — a design-thesis collapse, not a tuning issue, and no amount of vocabulary discipline in §4.2 repairs it.
severity_examples.scenario: Deploying Uncs as combat-XP-gaining equipped skills necessarily produces player behavior that ranks and optimizes Uncs by combat output, regardless of the no-rarity rule and non-extractive vocabulary.

severity_examples.condition: Shipping randomized-drop mechanics on real contested cultural-heritage objects creates reputational and ethical exposure that the E13 schema's technical sophistication does not by itself mitigate; this needs resolution before implementation, not after launch.
severity_examples.scenario: §9-D Option 1 (provenance-as-affix) is adopted without the doc first establishing what 'a good position on repatriation' — its own stated bar — actually requires in practice.

severity_examples.condition: This is a quality-of-experience risk that undermines the 'the recognition IS the reward' tone without breaking any explicit rule in the doc — flag as P2, not inflate to a blocking defect.
severity_examples.scenario: The Way-depth/orientation axes produce a de facto power curve (per the itemization reviewer's mechanical analysis) even without a declared rarity tier, and a community tier-list for Uncs emerges post-launch.

success_hints: Grounds claims about 'what players will actually do' in comparable shipped-game precedent (names specific games/mechanics) rather than asserting player psychology from first principles.

Treats 'the doc already names this as a risk' (§9-A's honest-risk paragraph, §6.1) as a starting point for testing whether the proposed mitigation is sufficient, not as evidence the concern is already handled.

Distinguishes mechanism-level compliance (no queryable field, no rarity tag) from outcome-level compliance (whether players actually end up treating Uncs/artifacts as extraction targets), and reviews on the latter.

Does not re-derive whether the canon clauses were read honestly, or whether the mechanics are buildable and balanced — focuses on whether the design philosophy survives contact with the mechanics as specified.
task_context: Stress-test this cross-repo game-design composition before mk ratifies it. Three concerns, in priority order. (1) The seven open calls in §9 — are the recommendations right, and is any 'ratified ruling' in §8 actually load-bearing enough to be an open call instead? (2) Ontology and canon compliance: the doc runs into uncrancher/docs/ontology.md §5 (Uncanny-as-unlock marked a PERMANENT v0 constraint; sitting-only play modes forbidden) and After-Them/docs/universe.md (canonical: 'Encryptids as skill-entities agents equip — none of this is renamed or restructured'). Are the proposed reconciliations honest readings or motivated ones? (3) Does the composition actually hold as a game — three tempos, Uncs as skills, artifacts as loot, inverted socket — or does it collapse under a failure mode the doc has not named? Especially: does R8's observation-not-collection thesis survive Uncs being deployed as combat abilities at all?
